title: Why your foot gets pins and needles
examples: Why does my foot fall asleep?
Why does my leg tingle after sitting?

stages.ask: Why does sitting on my leg make it go numb?

stages.label: Nerve squashed
stages.note: The nerve can't send its messages properly.

explain.say: Have you ever sat cross-legged for ages, then stood up and found your foot fizzing like a fizzy drink? That's pins and needles! Look at the first stage. When you sit on your leg, your weight presses on a nerve, a long wire that carries messages to your brain.

explain.say: See the wire? Squashed, the nerve can't carry its messages properly, and the blood vessels beside it are squeezed too, so the nerve gets less oxygen. Can you guess what your foot feels like now?

explain.say: Look at the shoe. Your foot goes numb, or sleepy. It might feel heavy, or you might feel almost nothing at all. People say: my foot's gone to sleep! Has your foot ever fallen asleep?

explain.say: Now you stand up and the pressure comes off. See the lightning? The nerve wakes up and fires lots of jumbled signals all at once. Your brain reads them as prickles, tingles and fizzing. The proper name is paraesthesia.

faq.q: Why does sitting on my leg make it go numb?
faq.a: Your weight presses on a nerve and the blood vessels beside it. The squashed nerve can't send messages properly, so your foot feels numb.
asks: Why does my foot fall asleep?

faq.q: Why does a waking foot tingle?
faq.a: When the pressure comes off, the nerve starts working again and fires lots of jumbled signals at once. Your brain reads them as prickling and fizzing.

faq.q: What is the proper name for pins and needles?
faq.a: Paraesthesia, which means an unusual feeling on the skin, like tingling or prickling.
The everyday kind, from sitting awkwardly, is harmless and goes away in a minute or two. If tingling keeps happening for no clear reason, it's worth asking a doctor.
asks: Is it bad when my foot falls asleep?

faq.q: Why does hitting my funny bone tingle?
faq.a: The funny bone isn't a bone but the ulnar nerve, which runs close to the skin at your elbow. Knocking it squashes the nerve and sends a zing down your arm.

facts: The medical term for pins and needles is paraesthesia.
The funny bone is really the ulnar nerve, passing close to the skin at the elbow.
